intro: Brunei is a small, oil-rich sultanate on the island of Borneo, once the centre of a powerful maritime empire.

chapters.title: A golden age
text: In the 1400s and 1500s the Sultanate of Brunei controlled coasts across Borneo and into the southern Philippines. The name Borneo itself may come from Brunei.
Its capital was a town built on stilts over the water, Kampong Ayer, which still exists.

chapters.title: Decline and British protection
text: Brunei lost land to Spain and to the British adventurer James Brooke, who became Rajah of Sarawak. In 1888 it became a British protectorate. Oil was found in 1929.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Brunei chose not to join Malaysia in 1963 and became fully independent in 1984. Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah has reigned since 1967, one of the longest reigns in the world.

keyTerms.meaning: A state ruled by a sultan.
A state protected and partly controlled by another.
